findings.explanation: module.helmrepo.tf:7 passes `log_bucket = ""` to the external terraform-gcp-storage module (pinned at ref 1739dfd1cc78c218fd744bbecf7d4c1b4eeef025). holden's deterministic scan can't see into that module's resource graph — it lives in another repo — but the parameter name and this author's other storage modules make it unambiguous: an empty log_bucket disables GCS access logging on the bucket that this module creates and serves publicly (via the caller-supplied `binding` IAM grant). This bucket hosts a Helm chart repository intended for external/public consumption (hence the accompanying robots.txt), so there is no audit trail of who fetched or attempted to fetch chart artifacts, and no way to detect abuse or enumeration. Because `log_bucket` is hardcoded rather than exposed as a variable on this module, no caller can turn logging on without forking the module.
findings.remediation: Add a `log_bucket` (or `enable_access_logging` + destination) input variable on this module, default to the current empty-string behavior for backward compatibility, and document that production/public deployments should set it to a real log sink bucket.
findings.title: Bucket access logging is explicitly disabled via a hardcoded empty log_bucket, with no way for callers to turn it on

findings.explanation: The file's entire content was the single line `“User-Agent: *nDisallow: /”` — curly/smart quotes wrapping the whole thing, with a literal letter `n` where the newline should be. Fixed to plain `User-Agent: *` / `Disallow: /` on separate lines.
findings.remediation: Replace template/robots.txt with plain ASCII, one directive per line: `User-Agent: *` followed by a real newline, then `Disallow: /`.
findings.title: robots.txt content is corrupted and will not actually disallow crawling as intended

findings.explanation: module.helmrepo.tf:2 pins `module.storage` to terraform-gcp-storage ref `1739dfd1` (`v0.4.0`). A local `.terraform/modules/storage` cache from earlier work let holden resolve into that module's actual source this one time, and it fires `HLD_GCP_001` (HIGH, encryption) — `google_storage_bucket.bucket` has no `encryption` block at all at this ref (confirmed by reading the module's source directly: `google_storage_bucket.bucket.tf` has zero `encryption`/`kms_key_name` wiring, and the `kms_key` variable is fully commented out in `variables.tf`). Under normal operation — a fresh checkout with no `.terraform` cache, which is how holden's CI-run scan of this repo actually operates — holden cannot fetch git-sourced module refs at all ("local module scan failed", confirmed at the start of this review chain) and silently reports zero findings for this entire subgraph. So this repo's own consumers get an unencrypted-by-CMEK bucket with no warning from any automated scan, even though the same author's terraform-gcp-storage repo already shipped a fix for exactly this at commit `e314472` (tag `v0.4.1`, `encryption { default_kms_key_name = var.kms_key_name }`), one commit past the currently-pinned ref. Since terraform-gcp-helmrepo's own `kms_key_name` variable (variables.tf) is now required with no default, wiring it through to `module.storage.kms_key_name` (which is also required, no default, in v0.4.1) is a direct, non-optional match — no design conflict this time (the earlier conflict, when this module's own kms_key_name was still optional, is gone now that it's required).
findings.fix:
module "storage" {
  source          = "git::https://github.com/JamesWoolfenden/terraform-gcp-storage.git?ref=e314472e46f4254b711269ee7b8983256ed861b8" #v0.4.1
  project         = data.google_project.pike.name
  bucket_name     = var.bucket_name
  binding_members = var.binding.binding_members
  binding_role    = var.binding.binding_role
  log_bucket      = ""
  kms_key_name    = var.kms_key_name
}
findings.remediation: Bump module.helmrepo.tf:2 to `ref=e314472e46f4254b711269ee7b8983256ed861b8 #v0.4.1`, add `kms_key_name = var.kms_key_name` to the module.storage block, and mark outputs.tf's `output "bucket"` `sensitive = true` (v0.4.1 marks that output sensitive upstream). Note: this also renames the bucket's internal resource address (`google_storage_bucket.bucket` → `.pike`) and the iam binding gains `count`, so the next real apply will show a destroy+recreate on those two resources — a one-time, expected state churn from the version bump, not a config error.
findings.title: The bucket this module actually creates has no CMEK — invisible to holden's normal scan because it can't resolve the git-sourced module reference

findings.explanation: Same root cause and same discovery mechanism as HOLDEN_AI_003: holden fired `HLD_GCP_385` (LOW, backup-and-recovery) against the vendored copy of `google_storage_bucket.bucket` at the pinned `v0.4.0` ref, which has no `soft_delete_policy` block at all. This is invisible to holden's normal (no-module-cache) scan of this repo for the same reason as HOLDEN_AI_003. Unlike the CMEK gap, the fix for this one is unconditional in the upstream module — `v0.4.1` adds `soft_delete_policy { retention_duration_seconds = 604800 }` directly on the bucket resource with no new variable required, so it's resolved by the exact same version bump as HOLDEN_AI_003, no additional wiring needed.
findings.fix: See HOLDEN_AI_003 — same module.storage source bump, no additional change.
findings.remediation: Same fix as HOLDEN_AI_003 — bumping module.helmrepo.tf:2 to the `v0.4.1` ref resolves this automatically, no separate change needed.
findings.title: The bucket this module actually creates has no soft-delete retention configured — same cross-module blind spot as HOLDEN_AI_003
